{{Short description|Species of flowering plant}} {{Speciesbox |image = Teline linifolia.jpg |genus = Genista |species = linifolia |authority = [[Carl Linnaeus|L.]] |synonyms = ''Cytisus linifolius''
''Teline linifolia'' }} [[File:Genista linifolia MHNT.BOT.2016.24.71.jpg|thumb|''Genista linifolia'' [[MHNT]]]] '''''Genista linifolia''''' is a species of [[Broom (shrub)|broom]] known by the common names '''Mediterranean broom''',{{PLANTS|id=GELI5|taxon=Genista linifolia|access-date=19 January 2016}} '''needle-leaved broom'''{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }} and '''flax broom'''. It is native to southwestern Europe, North Africa, and the [[Canary Islands]]. ==Description== This is a [[shrub]] with hairy green stems and branches which can exceed two meters in height. Its leaves are made up of tough, green, lance-shaped leaflets with woolly undersides. Flowers appear in dense raceme [[inflorescence]]s toward the ends of the branches. The flowers are bright yellow and pealike. The fruit is a hairy legume pod one to four centimeters long containing several seeds. ==Invasive plant species== It can be found on other continents in areas of similar [[Mediterranean climate]], such as [[California]] in the United States, Australia and New Zealand.
